newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Westpac says StanChart not predatory.
newsitem.headline: Westpac says StanChart not predatory.

text.p: Westpac Banking Corp executive David Morgan said on Thursday he did not believe the alliance with Standard Chartered Bank Plc would eventually lead to a takeover bid by the U.K.-based bank.
"I don't believe that it is their aspiration," Morgan told reporters after addressing a corporate treasury conference.
Westpac and Standard Chartered said on Wednesday they had formed a facility-sharing alliance in the Asia/Pacific region. The pact does not include any exchange of equity.
Morgan, the head of Westpac's institutional and banking group, negotiated the deal with Standard Chartered.
It was "one hundred percent incorrect" to believe that alliance was a defensive move by Westpac. "There was and is no defensive motivation for that strategy whatsoever," Morgan said.
But he also said he did not believe the alliance would necessarily protect Westpac from a takeover.
"I have not given that deep thought, but my initial reaction is to say I do not believe it would be a significant factor in debarring a takeover," he told reporters.
Westpac is one of Australia's four major private banks, with each having assets of more than A$100 billion and operations in each of Australia's six states.

The federal government currently opposes a merger of the big four banks with each other or with the two leading life offices but these principles are now under the microscope of the Wallis inquiry into the national financial system.
Morgan said the move to forge the alliance with Standard Chartered had been a race against time for a "huge first mover advantage" which would be difficult for other Australian banks to emulate.
He said Westpac had leapfrogged its opposition in terms of anything it could offer customers in Asia.
"It is our intention to grow this relationship over time," Morgan said.
He did not volunteer specific revenue or profit targets.

Westpac's main rivals at home and in the region are the two Melbourne-based banks, National Australia Bank Ltd and Australia and New Zealand Banking Group Ltd, and the fellow Sydney-based Commonwealth Bank of Australia.
